subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a moderately detailed truck module without relying on external catalogs, keeping it compact at around 250 parts and writing my own helper functions. I'll go with a simple structure: a root chassis joint, with wheels potentially using spin joints, since static models can skip joints if not needed.

I'm working out dimensions—truck length around 5.5 units, width 2.1, wheel radius near 0.45, positioned at the corners with proper ground clearance—and planning five SVG textures for decals, warning signs, a HUD screen, a door tag, and tail lights with glow effects on the lamps.

Defining geometry helpers and part-placement functions, then laying out the body structure with chassis rails, a lower body slab, and fender arches to cover the wheel wells where the wheels poke into the body.

Now I'm shaping the cab section with a raked windscreen, building its profile as a polygon of points across the z-y plane to get the angled front and roofline right.

I need to tilt the windscreen box by rotating about the x-axis so its normal faces up and forward correctly, computing the angle from the direction vector to get roughly 26.6 degrees, then offset it slightly outward along that normal.

Now I'm shaping the hood as a wedge extrusion with a profile that slopes from a tall rear section down toward the bumper, adding glow vent strips and ERA bricks on top. For the bed, I'm defining the floor and side walls with their dimensions, considering whether to add an armored bed cover with a turret mount.

I'm planning a roof-mounted turret with yaw/pitch joints carrying an autocannon and laser, plus bed-mounted glowing battery cylinders, antenna array, lightbar, and rear thrusters built via a lathe profile. I'm also working out the wheel construction with an armored disc, a 10-sided torus tire rotated on the X axis, bolts, and tread blocks arranged around the tire.

Setting up wheel joints with sideways-facing direction vectors, defining the chassis root joint, and establishing a color palette for the armor panels, trim, and glowing cyan/magenta/amber accents, including a custom worn-paint shader function.

I'm positioning textured plane decals for the cab doors on either side, figuring out plane placement near the extruded sides (~±0.9) and considering how facing direction affects whether the texture reads correctly from outside the vehicle.

Now I'm sketching out the helper function for placing colored geometry, then detailing the cab: door seams, handles, glass windows sized and positioned on the sides, roof slopes, mirrors with pods, and a lightbar with glowing amber lamps near the roof turret.

I'm placing the turret with yaw/pitch joints, a ring, cheek plates, and barrel cylinders, then moving to the bed structure with floor, side walls, glowing cyan battery cells, and rear thruster bells built as lathed shapes facing backward.

Now I'm adding the front bumper with ram teeth and winch, cyan headlight slits, a dark grille, and magenta underglow neon rods along the sides, plus an antenna whip and side skirt plates.

Working through wheel placement at z ±1.6 with radius .42, I'm adjusting fender boxes to sit flush over the wheels and tweaking the hood's width and height so it doesn't overlap the wheel tops, lowering the hood profile to clear the fenders properly.

Working out tyre tread placement by rotating small blocks around the wheel's axis so each tread segment sits tangentially at the correct angle along the tire's circumference.

Settling on five textures total—license plate, chevron bumper decal, neon sign, plus the warning details. Now I'm defining the turret's yaw and pitch joints with their positions and rotation axes, then sizing the barrel cylinder and placing it relative to the pitch joint.

I'm setting up helper functions for parts and cylinders to avoid repetition, mirroring symmetric elements across left/right sides, and adding a glow wrapper for the lamps. For the body panels I'm using extrude calls with outlines, bevels, and thickness to shape the hood and cab sections.

Writing neon rod code...
